text:
sam: Heads up — saw inconsistent exception shape from the Python SDK when the API returns a 400 with validation details.
elaine: can you paste the snippet where you call the client?
sam: sure:
```py
from redwood import RedwoodClient, ValidationError
client = RedwoodClient(api_key=... )
try:
    client.chat.create(...)
except ValidationError as e:
    print(e.errors)  # expecting structured errors
except Exception as e:
    print(type(e), e)
```
sam: Instead of ValidationError I got a generic HTTPError / APIError and the parsed payload was a raw string. stack snippet: `redwood.errors.APIError: 400 Bad Request - b"{\"detail\": \"Invalid input\"}"`
mike: oh — is this from the async client or sync? we've had a mismatch before where the async transport returned bytes and the sync one returned dicts.
sam: happened in both environments for me but repro was in an async FastAPI sample app calling `await client.chat.create(...)`.
nora: that's bad. We should absolutely normalize to a structured ValidationError (with .errors list, .status_code, .raw_body). Also the typing should expose the exception class so callers can `except ValidationError:`.
elaine: agreed. Current public docs show `ValidationError` in examples but the implementation sometimes surfaces `APIError`.
ci-bot: Created GitHub issue: https://github.com/redwood-inference/sdk-python/issues/542 (py-sdk: inconsistent error types + raw byte payload)
mike: thanks CI. Probable root cause: our HTTP layer decodes JSON only for `response.content_type == 'application/json'` but some infra returns `application/problem+json` or bytes and we fallback to raw bytes. Async client path didn't run the JSON parser in the error branch.
elaine: proposal: 1) add a parsing helper that tries json.loads on response body regardless of content_type (safe fallback), 2) canonicalize known keys (detail -> errors), 3) raise ValidationError with structured payload and keep .raw_body attached.
nora: +1. Also update types: exceptions.py should export `ValidationError` in the package `__all__` and stubs should include `.errors: List[str]` and `.status_code: int`. Add an `is_validation()` helper method?
mike: we can implement `ValidationError.errors: List[Dict[str,str]]` for field-level detail, and add `def is_validation(self) -> bool:` on base error to make checking easier for callers. Backwards compatibility: if code was catching APIError, we should keep APIError as baseclass and make ValidationError subclass it.
sam: filed the minimal reproduction in the GH issue comment with sample async snippet.
ci-bot: linked PR template in issue #542.
elaine: can we also add an example to the quickstart showing how to handle structured validation errors (sync + async)? People trip on this in onboarding.
mike: will take the PR. Plan: add tests for sync+async error parsing, update exceptions typing, docs snippet, and changelog entry. Target release 0.14.0.
nora: also remind infra to set response content-type consistently, but can't rely on it — good to be defensive.
sam: small nit — include the raw body as `e.raw_body` and the original response in `e.response` so advanced users can inspect headers.
mike: noted. I'll add `raw_body` (bytes) and `parsed_body` (optional[dict]) attributes, mark `raw_body` as bytes but in typeshed use `Any` for compatibility.
elaine: please add a short migration note in the release notes: `ValidationError` now subclass of `APIError` + new attributes `.errors` and `.raw_body`.
sam: thanks all :thumbsup:
elaine: assigning @mike. ping me when PR ready and I'll take docs/tests.
ci-bot: PR opened: https://github.com/redwood-inference/sdk-python/pull/678 (add structured ValidationError + async error parsing)
mike: PR created, tests added, drafted docs. will iterate on review.
sam: verified fix in local branch — async & sync both raise ValidationError now, `e.errors` populated. leaving final review to you @elaine.
elaine: thanks, merging after one more test. good catch.
